return_and_stair_review_2026_10_27.return_evidence: May 2011 close and corner panoramas plus the snag photograph: three lower windows and a door; four middle windows, with pairs separated by a broad central wall; upper centre opening smaller. Opening centres estimated along the 12m white return from photo proportions. Door threshold is local 0.12m (absolute 0.05m); its height follows the matched pavement rather than moving the entire building.
return_and_stair_review_2026_10_27.return_dimensions_m: Lower sill 0.55, height 1.75; middle sill 3.4, height 2.5; upper sill 8.5, height 2.1 except smaller centre. Door 1.25 wide by 2.22 high. Approximate dimensions and upper count, not survey.
return_and_stair_review_2026_10_27.stair_evidence: The August 2023 Mark Wellstern image resolves an outer 3/2/3 baluster rhythm along two sloping runs separated by a short flat section; the 2011 oblique view shows treads and supports. About 11 central landing balusters are visible; 16 risers per flight, eight on either side of a 0.85m middle landing, remain an estimate because the upper steps are partially occluded.
return_and_stair_review_2026_10_27.features: Retain exposed doorway and lower windows, paired middle sashes, small upper centre sash, rustication and a blank blue sign. Retain two physical stair flights and landings at every level; Detail/Walk keep cheek seats and balusters, District keeps the changing slope in its independent envelope.

ground: The building retains its level -0.07m architectural datum. The white return opens directly onto the north path. At site y=-29.72 the Christ Church approach now meets the adjoining church-garden rough plane (about -0.042m there) and follows it through y=-35; a bounded linear slope reaches the retained approach datum by y=-45. These heights are rough editable estimates, not a surveyed terrain model. The entrance stair remains on the separate Lord Street forecourt.
